question: The Manusmriti, one of the best-known legal texts of early India, is written in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __Sanskrit__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Manusmriti is usually translated as "code of Manu", but it literally means "reflections of Manu".
 
• It was written in Sanskrit.
 
• It presents itself as a document that compiles and organizes the code of conduct for human society.
 
• Manu-smriti is the popular name of the work, which is officially known as Manava-dharma-shastra.
 
• Manusmriti says that (1) Lord (king), (2) Minister, (3) Capital, (4) Rashtra, (5) Treasure, (6) Army (or force), and (7) Ally are the seven characteristics (Prakratis) of the state.
 
• It covers a wide range of topics such as the creation of the world, sacraments like ‘Upanayana’ and marriage; duties of men and women placed in different strata of society and stages of life; penitential rites for violation of codes of conduct; and so on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Manusmriti was one of the first Sanskrit texts studied by the European philologists.

 
 
• It was first translated into English by Sir William Jones.
 
• His version was published in 1794.
 
 
 
• Manusmriti is one of the most famous scriptural texts of early India. It is written in Sanskrit.
 
• Manavadharmashastra or Manusmriti belongs to the Dharmashastra literary tradition of Hinduism.
 
• It was composed between the 2nd century BCE and the 3rd century CE.
